taskVersion.name: ves-real-item

parts.text:
You are preparing a groundwater site note for a borehole drilling team.

Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station Kenpoly-sec-school-field, Bori Metropolis. Interpreted layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 1874 | 2.78 | 2.78
2 | 2428 | 9.13 | 11.9
3 | 1071 | 15.2 | 27.1
4 | 3706 | 32.2 | 59.3
5 | 178 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this station's curve as KHK-type.

Write a short site report (under 150 words) for station Kenpoly-sec-school-field, covering the layer sequence and the curve type. End with one JSON line exactly like this:
{"curve_type_stated": "<letters>", "label_issue_flagged": true or false}
Set label_issue_flagged to true only if your report says the curve-type classification on file does not fit the layer values.

**Site Report – Kenpoly-sec-school-field, Bori Metropolis**

The vertical electrical sounding at this station resolved a five-layer subsurface model. Resistivities increase from 1874 Ω·m (layer 1) to a maximum of 2428 Ω·m (layer 2), drop sharply to 1071 Ω·m (layer 3), rise again to a strong high of 3706 Ω·m (layer 4), and finally decrease to 178 Ω·m in the basal layer (layer 5), interpreted as the lowest-resistivity unit encountered, likely representing a conductive saturated zone or clay-rich material at depth (>59.3 m).

Applying the standard three-layer curve-type coding: layers 1-2-3 give K (r1<r2>r3), layers 2-3-4 give H (r2>r3<r4), and layers 3-4-5 give K (r3<r4>r5), yielding the sequence KHK. This matches the on-file classification, confirming the resistivity alternation pattern is correctly represented.

Recommend targeting the layer 3 and layer 5 zones for further hydrogeological evaluation given their comparatively low resistivity signatures.

{"curve_type_stated": "KHK", "label_issue_flagged": false}
